Both partners should understand the full financial picture and plan together
Keep all finances 100% separate — never share anything
Whoever earns more controls all decisions

pt-BR.explanation: Financial transparency and joint planning between partners leads to better decisions and fewer conflicts.

pt-BR.question: What is the most effective way to teach kids about money?

answers.text: Give them pocket money with no conditions
Let them observe — never discuss money with children
Give pocket money with saving rules (e.g. save 20%, spend 60%, give 20%)
Wait until they're 18 to discuss finances

pt-BR.explanation: Pocket money with saving/spending rules gives kids real financial decisions at low cost.

pt-BR.question: What inflation rate has the National Bank of Poland (NBP) targeted since 2004?

answers.text: Whatever the government sets each year

pt-BR.explanation: Since 2004 the NBP's target is 2.5% (±1 percentage point), measured by the annual change in the CPI.

pt-BR.question: Why do central banks aim for low, positive inflation (~2–2.5%) instead of 0%?

answers.text: To make the currency worthless faster
A small, stable buffer supports growth and avoids dangerous deflation
Because higher prices are always good
To increase government tax revenue only

pt-BR.explanation: A low, stable target avoids deflation (which can stall an economy) and keeps inflation predictable.

pt-BR.question: What is a central bank's main tool for steering inflation?
pt-BR.explanation: Central banks mainly use benchmark interest rates to influence borrowing, demand and ultimately inflation.

pt-BR.question: When a central bank raises interest rates, what typically happens?

answers.text: Borrowing gets cheaper and spending jumps
Borrowing gets more expensive, cooling demand and inflation

pt-BR.explanation: Rate hikes raise the cost of borrowing, which cools spending and helps bring inflation down.

pt-BR.question: What does GDP (Gross Domestic Product) measure?

answers.text: The total savings of all citizens
The value of all goods and services produced in an economy
The amount of cash in circulation

pt-BR.explanation: GDP = the total market value of goods and services produced in a country over a period.

pt-BR.question: Why is persistent deflation (falling prices) considered dangerous?

answers.text: It makes everyone richer with no downside
People delay purchases, demand drops, and debts get harder to repay
It has no effect on the economy

pt-BR.explanation: Deflation pushes people to delay spending and makes existing debt heavier in real terms — a dangerous loop.

pt-BR.question: What is 'zero-based budgeting'?

answers.text: Spending until your account hits zero
Giving every unit of income a job so income − all allocations = 0

pt-BR.explanation: Zero-based budgeting = assign every unit of income a job (spending, saving, debt) until the plan balances to zero.

pt-BR.question: What's the recommended first step before building a household budget?

answers.text: Track your actual spending for about 30 days
Take out a loan to cover gaps

pt-BR.explanation: Track spending for ~30 days first. You can't manage what you don't measure.

pt-BR.question: What is a 'sinking fund' in household budgeting?

answers.text: Cash set aside gradually for a known future expense

pt-BR.explanation: A sinking fund = saving a little each month for a planned future cost, so it doesn't become a shock.

pt-BR.question: What's an effective tactic against impulse spending?

answers.text: Buy now and decide later if you needed it
Use a waiting period (e.g. 24–72h, or 30 days for big buys) before non-essentials
Remove all prices so you don't notice

pt-BR.explanation: Add a waiting period before non-essential purchases — the pause defeats most impulse spending.

pt-BR.question: What's a realistic FIRST emergency-savings milestone if 3–6 months feels far away?

answers.text: Don't bother until you can save 6 months at once

pt-BR.explanation: Aim for one month of essentials first — research shows even a small buffer dramatically reduces delinquency.

pt-BR.question: In Poland, up to what amount are bank deposits guaranteed by the BFG?

answers.text: The PLN equivalent of €100,000 per depositor, per bank

pt-BR.explanation: Poland's BFG guarantees deposits up to the PLN equivalent of €100,000 per depositor in each bank.

pt-BR.question: What does 'asset allocation' mean?

answers.text: How you split investments among stocks, bonds and cash
Keeping everything in a checking account

pt-BR.explanation: Asset allocation = how you divide money across asset types (stocks, bonds, cash) to match your goals and risk.

pt-BR.question: What is portfolio 'rebalancing'?

answers.text: Periodically adjusting holdings back to your target mix

pt-BR.explanation: Rebalancing = restoring your target stock/bond/cash mix periodically, so risk doesn't drift.

pt-BR.question: Why do low ongoing fees (TER) matter so much for long-term investing?

answers.text: Fees compound against you and quietly erode decades of returns
Higher fees always mean higher returns

pt-BR.explanation: Fees compound against you. Over decades, even ~1% per year can erode a big share of your returns.

pt-BR.question: What is the general relationship between risk and expected return?

answers.text: Higher expected returns generally come with higher risk
High returns are guaranteed with zero risk
Lower risk always means higher return

pt-BR.explanation: Higher potential return generally requires taking on more risk. Be sceptical of 'high return, no risk' offers.

pt-BR.question: What should you generally have in place BEFORE investing in volatile assets?

answers.text: An emergency fund and high-interest debt under control

pt-BR.explanation: Before volatile investing: build an emergency fund and clear high-interest debt — that's your foundation.

pt-BR.question: How should beginners treat highly speculative assets like crypto?

answers.text: Put all savings in for maximum gains
Limit to a small share you could afford to lose entirely
Treat it as a safe emergency fund

pt-BR.explanation: Keep speculative assets to a small portion of your portfolio, and only money you can afford to lose completely.

pt-BR.question: What's the key tax difference between Poland's IKE and IKZE accounts?

answers.text: They are identical in every way
IKE: tax-free gains on a qualifying withdrawal; IKZE: deduct contributions now, pay a 10% flat tax on withdrawal
Both are taxed at 19% every year

pt-BR.explanation: IKE = tax-free growth on qualifying withdrawal. IKZE = deduct contributions today, 10% flat tax when you withdraw.

pt-BR.question: In Poland's PPK, what does the employer add on top of the employee's 2% basic contribution?

answers.text: A basic 1.5% of salary (plus an optional extra up to 2.5%)
A flat 100 PLN regardless of salary

pt-BR.explanation: PPK: employee 2% basic, employer adds 1.5% basic (up to +2.5% extra). The employer match is free retirement money.

pt-BR.question: What state incentives does Poland's PPK give participants?

answers.text: A 250 PLN welcome payment and a 240 PLN annual bonus

pt-BR.explanation: PPK state support: a one-off 250 PLN welcome payment and a 240 PLN annual bonus for participants.

pt-BR.question: What do deposit guarantee schemes (BFG, FDIC, EU DGS, FGC) actually protect?

answers.text: All investments including stocks and crypto
Bank deposits — not stocks, funds, pensions or crypto
Your salary if you lose your job

pt-BR.explanation: These schemes protect bank deposits only. Stocks, funds, pensions and crypto fall outside them.

pt-BR.question: In the United States, how much does the FDIC insure per depositor, per bank?

answers.text: There is no deposit insurance in the US

pt-BR.explanation: US FDIC coverage is $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each ownership category.

pt-BR.question: Across the EU (incl. Poland, Spain, France), bank deposits are guaranteed up to…

answers.text: €100,000 per depositor, per bank (or local-currency equivalent)
Nothing is guaranteed in the EU

pt-BR.explanation: EU rules harmonise deposit protection at €100,000 per depositor, per bank.

pt-BR.question: With a US 401(k) that offers an employer match, what's the smartest first move?

answers.text: Skip it — matches are a trick
Contribute at least enough to get the full employer match (free money)
Put it all into a single company stock

pt-BR.explanation: Always contribute enough to capture the full employer match — it's free money you can't get any other way.

pt-BR.question: What do a UK ISA, a Japanese NISA and a Polish IKE have in common?

answers.text: They are tax-advantaged accounts that shelter investment growth
They are types of credit card

pt-BR.explanation: ISA (UK), NISA (Japan) and IKE (Poland) are tax-advantaged accounts that shelter investment gains.

pt-BR.question: What inflation target does India's central bank (RBI) aim for?

answers.text: 4% with a ±2 percentage point tolerance band

pt-BR.explanation: India's RBI targets 4% inflation with a tolerance band of ±2 percentage points (2–6%).

pt-BR.question: O que é a regra de orçamento 50/30/20?
pt-BR.explanation: 50% para necessidades (aluguel, comida), 30% para desejos (lazer) e 20% para poupança e pagamento de dívidas. Simples e eficaz.

pt-BR.question: O que são juros compostos?

answers.text: Juros pagos só sobre o valor inicial
Uma tarifa bancária por saque antecipado
Juros ganhos sobre o principal e sobre os juros já acumulados
Juros que você paga apenas no cartão de crédito

pt-BR.explanation: Juros compostos significam ganhar juros sobre os seus juros; com o tempo isso gera crescimento exponencial. Dizem que Einstein os chamou de oitava maravilha do mundo.

pt-BR.question: O que significa 'diversificação' nos investimentos?

answers.text: Colocar todo o dinheiro em uma única ação forte
Distribuir os investimentos entre ativos diferentes para reduzir o risco

pt-BR.explanation: Não coloque todos os ovos na mesma cesta. A diversificação reduz o risco de um investimento ruim destruir a carteira inteira.

pt-BR.question: O que é a estratégia 'avalanche de dívidas'?

answers.text: Pegar novos empréstimos para pagar os antigos
Quitar primeiro as menores dívidas, sem olhar os juros
Quitar primeiro as dívidas com juros mais altos para minimizar o total de juros
Ignorar a dívida até ela crescer

pt-BR.explanation: Avalanche de dívidas = atacar primeiro os juros mais altos. Matematicamente é o que mais economiza dinheiro. É diferente da 'bola de neve', que começa pelos menores saldos para motivar.

pt-BR.question: Qual é o retorno real da sua poupança se a inflação é de 5% e o banco paga 2%?
pt-BR.explanation: Retorno real = taxa nominal − inflação = 2% − 5% = −3%. Seu dinheiro perde poder de compra mesmo em uma conta que rende 2%.

pt-BR.question: Que tipo de fundo acompanha automaticamente um índice de mercado com taxas baixas?
pt-BR.explanation: Fundos de índice e ETFs acompanham passivamente um índice de mercado (como o S&P 500). Têm taxas muito baixas e, historicamente, superam a maioria dos fundos de gestão ativa.

pt-BR.question: O que é o método de aportes regulares (DCA)?

answers.text: Comprar tudo na mínima do mercado
Vender tudo quando os preços caem
Investir um valor fixo em intervalos regulares, seja qual for o preço
Converter toda a poupança em dólares

pt-BR.explanation: DCA é investir o mesmo valor fixo todo mês, seja qual for o preço. Você compra mais quando os preços estão baixos e menos quando estão altos, tirando a emoção do investimento.

pt-BR.question: O que é a 'regra do 72'?

answers.text: Você precisa de 72 meses para quitar qualquer dívida
Dividir 72 pelo retorno anual para estimar em quantos anos o dinheiro dobra
Aposentar-se aos 72 para maximizar a aposentadoria

pt-BR.explanation: 72 ÷ retorno anual em % = anos para dobrar o dinheiro. Com 8%, o dinheiro dobra em cerca de 9 anos. Com 6%, em cerca de 12. Um truque rápido de conta de cabeça.

pt-BR.question: O que é um ETF?

answers.text: Uma conta poupança com juros maiores
Fundo negociado em bolsa: uma cesta de ativos negociada como uma ação
Um fundo de emergência do governo

pt-BR.explanation: Os ETFs reúnem muitos ativos (ações, títulos, commodities) em um único instrumento negociável. Combinam a diversificação de um fundo com a flexibilidade de uma ação.

pt-BR.question: Qual NÃO é uma característica de uma boa reserva de emergência?

answers.text: Cobre de 3 a 6 meses de despesas
Investida em ações de alto risco para crescer o máximo
Separada da conta de gastos do dia a dia

pt-BR.explanation: Uma reserva de emergência deve ser líquida e segura, NÃO investida em ativos voláteis. O objetivo é estar disponível quando a emergência surge, não crescer.

pt-BR.question: O que acontece com os preços dos títulos quando os juros sobem?
pt-BR.explanation: Títulos e juros se movem em sentidos opostos. Quando os juros sobem, os títulos existentes com taxas menores ficam menos atraentes e seu preço de mercado cai.

pt-BR.question: O que é 'inflação do estilo de vida'?

answers.text: O governo aumentar o salário mínimo
Preços subindo mais rápido que os salários
Gastar mais à medida que você ganha mais, sem aumentar a poupança
Inflar seu estilo de vida no currículo

pt-BR.explanation: Inflação do estilo de vida significa que cada aumento de salário é consumido por novas despesas. O antídoto: poupar o aumento antes de se acostumar com a renda extra.

pt-BR.question: Qual é o principal objetivo de uma conta de previdência/aposentadoria?

answers.text: Substituir a renda quando você parar de trabalhar, usando décadas de juros compostos
Especular com ativos de alto risco

pt-BR.explanation: Contas de aposentadoria são instrumentos de longo prazo. Os aportes crescem por décadas com vantagens fiscais. O tempo é o seu maior ativo: começar aos 25 em vez de aos 35 pode significar o dobro do saldo final.

pt-BR.question: O que significa 'patrimônio líquido'?

answers.text: Seu salário mensal depois dos impostos
Total de ativos menos total de dívidas
Quanto dinheiro você tem na carteira

pt-BR.explanation: Patrimônio líquido = tudo o que você tem (ativos) menos tudo o que você deve (passivos). Um patrimônio líquido positivo e crescente é a verdadeira medida da saúde financeira, mais significativa do que a renda sozinha.

pt-BR.question: Segundo dados da OCDE, que porcentagem dos poloneses entende corretamente os juros compostos?
pt-BR.explanation: Apenas cerca de 1 em cada 3 poloneses entende juros compostos na prática. É a lacuna de conhecimento número 1: leva a espirais de dívida e explica por que só 47% dos funcionários aderem aos planos voluntários de previdência PPK/PPE.

pt-BR.question: Que porcentagem dos poloneses confiava em instituições financeiras para a poupança em 2022?
pt-BR.explanation: Apenas 15% dos poloneses confiavam em instituições financeiras em 2022, e em 2021 esse número havia caído para 6%. Esse déficit de confiança é uma grande barreira à participação financeira e à construção de patrimônio no longo prazo.

pt-BR.question: A Polônia fez 13/21 em competência financeira da OCDE. O que a pontuação que falta representa?

answers.text: Oportunidades perdidas de acumular patrimônio e falta de preparo financeiro
Uma barreira de idioma no teste da OCDE

pt-BR.explanation: Os 13/21 colocam a Polônia no meio da tabela. Os 8 pontos que faltam representam oportunidades concretas perdidas: uso menos eficaz do mercado de capitais, menos reservas de emergência e mais vulnerabilidade a choques econômicos.

pt-BR.question: Quase metade dos poloneses diz que as finanças controlam sua vida. Qual é a mudança de mentalidade recomendada?

answers.text: Ganhar mais dinheiro a qualquer custo
Evitar pensar em dinheiro para reduzir o estresse
Recuperar a sensação de controle pessoal: tratar o dinheiro como ferramenta, não como fonte de estresse
Deixar um consultor financeiro cuidar de tudo

pt-BR.explanation: O pensamento de curto prazo é uma defesa psicológica quando a pessoa sente que não tem controle. A educação financeira precisa devolver essa sensação de controle, transformando o dinheiro de fonte de estresse em ferramenta de autonomia.

pt-BR.question: Qual conceito polonês descreve um colchão financeiro de emergência?
pt-BR.explanation: 'Poduszka finansowa' (almofada financeira) é o termo polonês para reserva de emergência. É um componente central do bem-estar financeiro: uma rede de segurança para absorver imprevistos sem recorrer a empréstimos com juros altos.

pt-BR.question: A OCDE constatou que apenas 26,9% dos poloneses atingem a nota mínima de atitude financeira. O que a 'atitude financeira' mede?

answers.text: Quantos produtos financeiros a pessoa tem
O nível de renda e a taxa de poupança
Se a pessoa planeja o futuro ou vive apenas o presente
O nível de confiança nos bancos

pt-BR.explanation: A atitude financeira mede a orientação para planejar o futuro em vez de pensar só no presente. Os 26,9% são cerca de metade da média da OCDE e refletem uma cultura sistêmica de pensamento financeiro de curto prazo.

tr.question: Acil durum fonu kaç aylık gideri karşılamalıdır?
tr.explanation: Acil durum fonu genellikle 3 ila 6 aylık temel giderleri karşılar.

tr.question: Hangi tasarruf alışkanlığı en etkilidir?

answers.text: Maaş gelince sabit tutarı otomatik aktarmak

tr.explanation: En etkili alışkanlık, gelir gelir gelmez otomatik aktarım yapmaktır.

tr.question: Faizler yükselince değişken faizli kredide ne olur?
tr.explanation: Değişken faizli krediler piyasa faizlerine bağlıdır; ödeme artabilir.

tr.question: What is 'net worth'?

answers.text: How much cash you have in your wallet

tr.explanation: Net worth is assets minus liabilities at the same date. Income is a flow; cash and credit scores are different measures. Net worth alone does not describe liquidity or your value as a person.

tr.question: What is 'lifestyle inflation'?

answers.text: Choosing more discretionary spending as your income rises
Inflating your lifestyle on your resume

tr.explanation: Lifestyle inflation is a voluntary rise in discretionary spending as income grows. It is different from price inflation or necessary expenses, and it does not mean every raise is fully spent.

tr.question: What does 'pay yourself first' mean?

answers.text: Spend on yourself before paying bills
Plan affordable savings after reserving money for essentials and required minimum payments

tr.explanation: First reserve money for essentials and required minimum payments, then choose savings from available surplus before discretionary spending. A transfer is optional; no surplus means no transfer, without blame.

tr.question: With PLN 4,000 take-home income, what is the illustrative 20% bucket?
tr.explanation: 4,000 × 20% = PLN 800. In this example, required minimum debt payments are included once in needs; the 20% bucket is savings and extra debt repayment. This is our illustration convention, not a compulsory split.

tr.question: Which checklist is most complete when comparing savings accounts in Poland?

answers.text: Rates and conditions, fees, access, and deposit protection
Whether the account guarantees an inflation-beating return
Whether your deposit is automatically invested in stocks

tr.explanation: Check the rate and its duration, qualifying conditions, fees, withdrawal access, and the applicable deposit guarantee scheme. A deposit account is not a stock investment; inflation can still reduce purchasing power.

tr.question: You invest PLN 100 twice, at PLN 10 then PLN 20 per unit. What do you buy?
tr.explanation: 100 ÷ 10 = 10 units; 100 ÷ 20 = 5 units. DCA uses equal amounts at regular intervals, not equal unit counts. At PLN 8 per unit, all 15 units are worth PLN 120 against PLN 200 invested: a PLN 80 loss, ignoring fees and taxes.

tr.question: What is the 'debt avalanche' strategy?

answers.text: Taking new loans to pay old loans
Paying off smallest debts first regardless of interest rate
Paying off highest-interest debts first to minimize total interest

tr.explanation: Debt avalanche: pay off highest-interest debt first. Saves the most money overall.

tr.question: Which factor has the BIGGEST impact on your credit score?

answers.text: Number of credit cards you own

tr.explanation: Payment history accounts for ~35% of a credit score. Paying on time, every time, is the #1 driver.

tr.question: What happens to bond prices when interest rates rise?
tr.explanation: Bonds and interest rates are inversely related: rates up → bond prices down.

tr.question: Which is NOT a characteristic of a good emergency fund?

answers.text: Invested in high-risk stocks for maximum growth
Kept separate from everyday spending account

tr.explanation: An emergency fund must be liquid and low-risk. High-risk stocks defeat the purpose.

tr.question: If 3–6 months seems too hard, what is the recommended first milestone?
tr.explanation: One month of essential expenses is the first realistic milestone for an emergency fund.

tr.question: What is compound interest?

answers.text: Interest paid only on the original amount
A bank fee for early withdrawal
Interest earned on both principal and previously earned interest
Interest you pay on credit cards only

tr.explanation: Compound interest: you earn interest on your interest — creates exponential growth over time.

tr.question: What does 'diversification' mean in investing?

answers.text: Putting all your money in one strong stock
Spreading investments across different assets to reduce risk

tr.explanation: Diversification = spreading money across different assets to reduce risk.

tr.question: Which type of fund tracks a market index automatically with low fees?
tr.explanation: Index funds / ETFs passively track an index (like S&P 500) with low fees.

tr.question: What is an ETF?

answers.text: A savings account with higher interest
Exchange-Traded Fund — a basket of assets traded like a stock

tr.explanation: ETF = Exchange-Traded Fund. A basket of assets you can buy/sell like a single stock.

tr.question: Studies show that for long-term investors, which strategy tends to outperform?

answers.text: Timing the market (buy low, sell high perfectly)
Staying invested consistently over time ('time in the market')

tr.explanation: Time in market beats timing the market. Consistent, patient investing outperforms most active strategies.

tr.question: What is the primary purpose of a retirement account?

answers.text: To replace income when you stop working, using decades of compounding

tr.explanation: Retirement accounts are long-term compounding vehicles. Time is the biggest asset — start early.

tr.question: If you invest $200/month at 7% annual return starting at age 25, approximately how much will you have at 65?
tr.explanation: 40 years of $200/month at 7% = ~$525,000. The power of time and compounding is extraordinary.

tr.question: According to OECD data, what percentage of Poles correctly understand how compound interest works?
tr.explanation: Only ~33% of Poles correctly understand compound interest — the OECD data confirms this critical knowledge gap.

tr.question: In 2022, what percentage of Poles trusted financial institutions for savings and investments?
tr.explanation: Only 15% of Poles trusted financial institutions in 2022. The 2021 low was just 6% — a profound trust deficit.

tr.question: What did Poland score on the OECD Financial Competency index?
tr.explanation: Poland scored 13/21 on the OECD Financial Competency index. The gap to maximum represents real lost savings.

tr.question: What percentage of employees in large Polish firms participate in the voluntary PPK/PPE pension scheme?
tr.explanation: Only 47% of employees in large Polish firms use voluntary PPK/PPE schemes — a direct consequence of compound interest illiteracy.

tr.question: Financial well-being is measured by three components. Which set is correct?

answers.text: Savings rate, credit score, net worth

tr.explanation: Financial well-being = Control over daily expenses + Safety Net (poduszka finansowa) + Future Goals like retirement.

tr.question: How is 'financial resilience' defined by Poland's National Financial Education Strategy?

answers.text: The ability to absorb financial shocks and recover from a difficult material situation
Owning property and having no debt

tr.explanation: Resilience = ability to deal with adverse financial shocks and recover. It's about preparedness, not wealth level.

tr.question: What is the primary financial literacy gap that leads to 'debt spirals'?

answers.text: Not knowing how to use a credit card
Not understanding compound interest — debt grows faster than expected

tr.explanation: Debt spirals are caused by not understanding compound interest — people underestimate how fast unpaid interest accumulates.

tr.question: What is the main purpose of life insurance?

answers.text: To get rich when someone dies
To replace income for dependents if the primary earner dies
To invest in the stock market safely

tr.explanation: Life insurance protects dependents by replacing the primary earner's income if they die prematurely.

tr.question: What is the recommended approach to finances for couples?

answers.text: One partner handles all finances, the other doesn't need to know
Both partners should understand the full financial picture and plan together
Keep all finances 100% separate — never share anything
Whoever earns more controls all decisions

tr.explanation: Financial transparency and joint planning between partners leads to better decisions and fewer conflicts.

tr.question: What is the most effective way to teach kids about money?

answers.text: Give them pocket money with no conditions
Let them observe — never discuss money with children
Give pocket money with saving rules (e.g. save 20%, spend 60%, give 20%)
Wait until they're 18 to discuss finances

tr.explanation: Pocket money with saving/spending rules gives kids real financial decisions at low cost.

tr.question: What inflation rate has the National Bank of Poland (NBP) targeted since 2004?

answers.text: Whatever the government sets each year

tr.explanation: Since 2004 the NBP's target is 2.5% (±1 percentage point), measured by the annual change in the CPI.

tr.question: Why do central banks aim for low, positive inflation (~2–2.5%) instead of 0%?

answers.text: To make the currency worthless faster
A small, stable buffer supports growth and avoids dangerous deflation
Because higher prices are always good
To increase government tax revenue only

tr.explanation: A low, stable target avoids deflation (which can stall an economy) and keeps inflation predictable.

tr.question: What is a central bank's main tool for steering inflation?
tr.explanation: Central banks mainly use benchmark interest rates to influence borrowing, demand and ultimately inflation.

tr.question: When a central bank raises interest rates, what typically happens?

answers.text: Borrowing gets cheaper and spending jumps
Borrowing gets more expensive, cooling demand and inflation

tr.explanation: Rate hikes raise the cost of borrowing, which cools spending and helps bring inflation down.

tr.question: What does GDP (Gross Domestic Product) measure?

answers.text: The total savings of all citizens
The value of all goods and services produced in an economy
The amount of cash in circulation

tr.explanation: GDP = the total market value of goods and services produced in a country over a period.

tr.question: Why is persistent deflation (falling prices) considered dangerous?

answers.text: It makes everyone richer with no downside
People delay purchases, demand drops, and debts get harder to repay
It has no effect on the economy

tr.explanation: Deflation pushes people to delay spending and makes existing debt heavier in real terms — a dangerous loop.

tr.question: What is 'zero-based budgeting'?

answers.text: Spending until your account hits zero
Giving every unit of income a job so income − all allocations = 0

tr.explanation: Zero-based budgeting = assign every unit of income a job (spending, saving, debt) until the plan balances to zero.

tr.question: What's the recommended first step before building a household budget?

answers.text: Track your actual spending for about 30 days
Take out a loan to cover gaps

tr.explanation: Track spending for ~30 days first. You can't manage what you don't measure.

tr.question: What is a 'sinking fund' in household budgeting?

answers.text: Cash set aside gradually for a known future expense

tr.explanation: A sinking fund = saving a little each month for a planned future cost, so it doesn't become a shock.

tr.question: What's an effective tactic against impulse spending?

answers.text: Buy now and decide later if you needed it
Use a waiting period (e.g. 24–72h, or 30 days for big buys) before non-essentials
Remove all prices so you don't notice

tr.explanation: Add a waiting period before non-essential purchases — the pause defeats most impulse spending.

tr.question: What's a realistic FIRST emergency-savings milestone if 3–6 months feels far away?

answers.text: Don't bother until you can save 6 months at once

tr.explanation: Aim for one month of essentials first — research shows even a small buffer dramatically reduces delinquency.

tr.question: In Poland, up to what amount are bank deposits guaranteed by the BFG?

answers.text: The PLN equivalent of €100,000 per depositor, per bank

tr.explanation: Poland's BFG guarantees deposits up to the PLN equivalent of €100,000 per depositor in each bank.

tr.question: What does 'asset allocation' mean?

answers.text: How you split investments among stocks, bonds and cash
Keeping everything in a checking account

tr.explanation: Asset allocation = how you divide money across asset types (stocks, bonds, cash) to match your goals and risk.

tr.question: What is portfolio 'rebalancing'?

answers.text: Periodically adjusting holdings back to your target mix

tr.explanation: Rebalancing = restoring your target stock/bond/cash mix periodically, so risk doesn't drift.

tr.question: Why do low ongoing fees (TER) matter so much for long-term investing?

answers.text: Fees compound against you and quietly erode decades of returns
Higher fees always mean higher returns

tr.explanation: Fees compound against you. Over decades, even ~1% per year can erode a big share of your returns.

tr.question: What is the general relationship between risk and expected return?

answers.text: Higher expected returns generally come with higher risk
High returns are guaranteed with zero risk
Lower risk always means higher return

tr.explanation: Higher potential return generally requires taking on more risk. Be sceptical of 'high return, no risk' offers.

tr.question: What should you generally have in place BEFORE investing in volatile assets?

answers.text: An emergency fund and high-interest debt under control

tr.explanation: Before volatile investing: build an emergency fund and clear high-interest debt — that's your foundation.

tr.question: How should beginners treat highly speculative assets like crypto?

answers.text: Put all savings in for maximum gains
Limit to a small share you could afford to lose entirely
Treat it as a safe emergency fund

tr.explanation: Keep speculative assets to a small portion of your portfolio, and only money you can afford to lose completely.

tr.question: What's the key tax difference between Poland's IKE and IKZE accounts?

answers.text: They are identical in every way
IKE: tax-free gains on a qualifying withdrawal; IKZE: deduct contributions now, pay a 10% flat tax on withdrawal
Both are taxed at 19% every year

tr.explanation: IKE = tax-free growth on qualifying withdrawal. IKZE = deduct contributions today, 10% flat tax when you withdraw.

tr.question: In Poland's PPK, what does the employer add on top of the employee's 2% basic contribution?

answers.text: A basic 1.5% of salary (plus an optional extra up to 2.5%)
A flat 100 PLN regardless of salary

tr.explanation: PPK: employee 2% basic, employer adds 1.5% basic (up to +2.5% extra). The employer match is free retirement money.

tr.question: What state incentives does Poland's PPK give participants?

answers.text: A 250 PLN welcome payment and a 240 PLN annual bonus

tr.explanation: PPK state support: a one-off 250 PLN welcome payment and a 240 PLN annual bonus for participants.

tr.question: What do deposit guarantee schemes (BFG, FDIC, EU DGS, FGC) actually protect?

answers.text: All investments including stocks and crypto
Bank deposits — not stocks, funds, pensions or crypto
Your salary if you lose your job

tr.explanation: These schemes protect bank deposits only. Stocks, funds, pensions and crypto fall outside them.

tr.question: In the United States, how much does the FDIC insure per depositor, per bank?

answers.text: There is no deposit insurance in the US

tr.explanation: US FDIC coverage is $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each ownership category.

tr.question: Across the EU (incl. Poland, Spain, France), bank deposits are guaranteed up to…

answers.text: €100,000 per depositor, per bank (or local-currency equivalent)
Nothing is guaranteed in the EU

tr.explanation: EU rules harmonise deposit protection at €100,000 per depositor, per bank.

tr.question: With a US 401(k) that offers an employer match, what's the smartest first move?

answers.text: Skip it — matches are a trick
Contribute at least enough to get the full employer match (free money)
Put it all into a single company stock

tr.explanation: Always contribute enough to capture the full employer match — it's free money you can't get any other way.

tr.question: What do a UK ISA, a Japanese NISA and a Polish IKE have in common?

answers.text: They are tax-advantaged accounts that shelter investment growth
They are types of credit card

tr.explanation: ISA (UK), NISA (Japan) and IKE (Poland) are tax-advantaged accounts that shelter investment gains.

tr.question: What inflation target does India's central bank (RBI) aim for?

answers.text: 4% with a ±2 percentage point tolerance band

tr.explanation: India's RBI targets 4% inflation with a tolerance band of ±2 percentage points (2–6%).

tr.question: 50/30/20 bütçe kuralı nedir?
tr.explanation: %50 ihtiyaçlara (kira, yemek), %30 isteklere (eğlence), %20 birikime ve borç ödemeye. Basit ve etkili.

tr.question: Bileşik getiri (bileşik faiz) nedir?

answers.text: Yalnızca ana para üzerinden ödenen faiz
Hem ana para hem de önceden kazanılan faiz üzerinden kazanılan faiz

tr.explanation: Bileşik faiz, faizinin de faiz kazanması demektir; zamanla bu üstel bir büyüme yaratır. Einstein'ın buna dünyanın sekizinci harikası dediği söylenir.

tr.question: Yatırımda 'çeşitlendirme' ne demektir?

answers.text: Tüm parayı tek bir güçlü hisseye yatırmak
Riski azaltmak için yatırımları farklı varlıklara yaymak

tr.explanation: Bütün yumurtaları aynı sepete koyma. Çeşitlendirme, tek bir kötü yatırımın tüm portföyünü yok etme riskini azaltır.

tr.question: 'Borç çığı' stratejisi nedir?

answers.text: Eski kredileri ödemek için yeni kredi çekmek
Faiz oranına bakmadan önce en küçük borçları ödemek
Toplam faizi en aza indirmek için önce en yüksek faizli borçları ödemek

tr.explanation: Borç çığı = önce en yüksek faiz oranına saldır. Matematiksel olarak en çok parayı bu yöntem kazandırır. Motivasyon için en küçük bakiyeleri hedefleyen 'borç kartopu'ndan farklıdır.

tr.question: Enflasyon %5 ve bankan %2 veriyorsa birikiminin reel getirisi nedir?
tr.explanation: Reel getiri = nominal oran − enflasyon = %2 − %5 = −%3. %2 faizli bir birikim hesabında bile paran alım gücü kaybediyor.

tr.question: Hangi fon türü bir piyasa endeksini düşük ücretlerle otomatik olarak izler?
tr.explanation: Endeks fonları ve ETF'ler bir piyasa endeksini (S&P 500 gibi) pasif olarak izler. Ücretleri çok düşüktür ve tarihsel olarak aktif yönetilen fonların çoğundan daha iyi performans göstermiştir.

tr.question: Düzenli yatırım (DCA) nedir?

answers.text: Fiyat ne olursa olsun düzenli aralıklarla sabit bir tutar yatırmak

tr.explanation: DCA, fiyat ne olursa olsun her ay aynı sabit tutarı yatırmaktır. Fiyatlar düşükken daha çok, yüksekken daha az alırsın; böylece duygu yatırımdan çıkar.

tr.question: '72 kuralı' nedir?

answers.text: Herhangi bir borcu ödemek için 72 ay gerekir
Paranın kaç yılda ikiye katlanacağını tahmin etmek için 72'yi yıllık getiri oranına böl
Emekli maaşını en üste çıkarmak için 72 yaşında emekli ol

tr.explanation: 72 ÷ yıllık getiri % = paranın ikiye katlanma süresi (yıl). %8 getiriyle paran yaklaşık 9 yılda ikiye katlanır. %6 ile yaklaşık 12 yılda. Hızlı bir zihinden hesap yöntemi.

tr.question: ETF nedir?

answers.text: Daha yüksek faizli bir birikim hesabı
Borsa yatırım fonu: hisse gibi işlem gören bir varlık sepeti

tr.explanation: ETF'ler birçok varlığı (hisse, tahvil, emtia) alınıp satılabilen tek bir araçta toplar. Bir fonun çeşitlendirmesini bir hissenin esnekliğiyle birleştirir.

tr.question: Hangisi iyi bir acil durum fonunun özelliği DEĞİLDİR?

answers.text: En yüksek büyüme için yüksek riskli hisselere yatırılmıştır

tr.explanation: Acil durum fonu likit ve güvenli olmalıdır; oynak varlıklara yatırılmamalıdır. Amacı büyümek değil, acil durumda erişilebilir olmaktır.

tr.question: Faizler yükseldiğinde tahvil fiyatlarına ne olur?
tr.explanation: Tahviller ve faizler ters yönde hareket eder. Faizler yükseldiğinde daha düşük faizli mevcut tahviller daha az cazip hale gelir ve piyasa fiyatları düşer.

tr.question: 'Yaşam tarzı enflasyonu' nedir?

answers.text: Kazandıkça daha çok harcamak ve birikimi aynı bırakmak

tr.explanation: Yaşam tarzı enflasyonu, her maaş artışının yeni giderlerle tüketilmesi demektir. Çaresi: ek gelire alışmadan önce zammı biriktirmek.

tr.question: Emeklilik hesabının temel amacı nedir?

answers.text: On yılların bileşik getirisini kullanarak çalışmayı bıraktığında gelirin yerini tutmak

tr.explanation: Emeklilik hesapları uzun vadeli araçlardır. Katkılar on yıllar boyunca vergi avantajıyla büyür. Zaman en büyük varlığındır: 35 yerine 25 yaşında başlamak nihai bakiyeyi iki katına çıkarabilir.

tr.question: 'Net varlık' ne demektir?
tr.explanation: Net varlık = sahip olduğun her şey (varlıklar) eksi borçlu olduğun her şey (yükümlülükler). Pozitif ve büyüyen net varlık, finansal sağlığın gerçek ölçüsüdür; tek başına gelirden daha anlamlıdır.

tr.question: OECD verilerine göre Polonyalıların yüzde kaçı bileşik faizi doğru anlıyor?
tr.explanation: Polonyalıların yalnızca yaklaşık üçte biri bileşik faizi pratikte anlıyor. Bu bir numaralı bilgi boşluğu: borç sarmallarına yol açıyor ve çalışanların neden yalnızca %47'sinin gönüllü PPK/PPE emeklilik planlarına katıldığını açıklıyor.

tr.question: 2022'de Polonyalıların yüzde kaçı birikimleri için finans kurumlarına güveniyordu?
tr.explanation: 2022'de Polonyalıların yalnızca %15'i finans kurumlarına güveniyordu; 2021'de bu oran %6'ya kadar düşmüştü. Bu güven açığı, finansal katılımın ve uzun vadeli servet birikiminin önündeki büyük bir engel.

tr.question: Polonya, OECD Finansal Yeterlilik'te 13/21 aldı. Eksik puan neyi temsil ediyor?

answers.text: Servet biriktirmede kaçırılan fırsatları ve finansal hazırlık eksikliğini

tr.explanation: 13/21 Polonya'yı sıralamanın ortasına yerleştiriyor. Eksik 8 puan somut kayıp fırsatlar demek: sermaye piyasalarının daha az etkili kullanımı, daha düşük acil durum fonu oranları ve ekonomik şoklara karşı daha fazla kırılganlık.

tr.question: Polonyalıların neredeyse yarısı hayatını finansının yönettiğini söylüyor. Önerilen zihniyet değişimi nedir?

answers.text: Ne pahasına olursa olsun daha çok para kazanmak
Stresi azaltmak için parayı düşünmekten kaçınmak

Her şeyi bir finans danışmanına bırakmak

en.title: What inflation means
en.body: Inflation means money buys less over time. The same amount covers fewer groceries, or the same rent costs more. Rising prices are the usual sign. Cash that sits still loses purchasing power.

en.title: Real return
en.body: Real return is the interest you earn minus inflation. If inflation is 5% and the bank pays 2%, the real return is about −3%. The balance can rise while its buying power falls. The rate on the account is not the whole story.

en.title: The rule of 72
en.body: The rule of 72 estimates how long money takes to double. Divide 72 by the yearly return. At 8% a year, money doubles in about 9 years. At 6%, it takes about 12 years.

en.title: A long-term hedge
en.body: A hedge is something that has tended to grow faster than prices. Broad stock index funds have done that over many years. Cash under a mattress and a 1% savings account have not. The point is a long horizon, not a quick bet.

pl.title: Co znaczy inflacja
pl.body: Inflacja znaczy, że z czasem za te same pieniądze kupisz mniej. Ta sama kwota starczy na mniej zakupów, a ten sam czynsz kosztuje więcej. Ceny idą w górę. Gotówka, która leży bez ruchu, traci siłę nabywczą.

pl.title: Realna stopa zwrotu
pl.body: Realna stopa zwrotu to oprocentowanie minus inflacja. Jak inflacja wynosi 5%, a bank daje 2%, wychodzi około −3%. Na koncie może przybywać złotówek, a i tak kupisz za nie mniej. Samo oprocentowanie nie mówi, czy naprawdę zarabiasz.

pl.title: Reguła 72
pl.body: Reguła 72 podpowiada, po ilu latach pieniądze się podwoją. Dzielisz 72 przez roczną stopę zwrotu. Przy 8% rocznie wychodzi około 9 lat. Przy 6% około 12 lat.

pl.title: Ochrona na lata
pl.body: Dobra ochrona przed inflacją to coś, co przez lata rosło szybciej niż ceny. Tak było z szerokimi funduszami indeksowymi akcji. Gotówka pod materacem i konto na 1% tak nie działają. Liczy się długi czas, nie szybki zysk.
